findings.reason: the builder must be told the context verdict is absent for this candidate and must compute it in the waiver pass; a literal implementation of the words "re-judges each reserved candidate with the tier and attempts terms waived" leaves the offered lane unchecked and the fourth case failing for a reason the section does not name.
findings.text: §55 says "The lane's window ceiling and its budget verdict still apply, and so does its own context fit, {at the re-judge}", but on the waiver path the reserved candidate's context fit has never been measured: `_fit()` is called only inside `if not reasons:` (`reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:1630-1636`), and a reserved lane reaches that line with its tier reason already appended (`:1627-1629`), so `context` stays `None` and `context_block` stays `None` for exactly the candidate the waiver re-judges; re-judging the policy alone therefore offers a candidate whose context fit is unknown, and the fourth done-when case ("not offered a reserved lane whose own window it also exceeds") cannot be satisfied without also running `_fit` and populating the context block on that path

findings.reason: the qualifier is the whole safety of an elevated-risk change on the picker's hot path; without a case for it the gate cannot tell the narrow waiver the deliverable states from the broad one, and the broad one spends a reserved lane on nodes excluded for reasons the waiver was never meant to override.
findings.text: §55's waiver fires only "when the set has no unreserved candidate left **and each unreserved one was excluded only on `context-fit`**", but the four cases test the first clause only: case 2 (node within the local window) makes the local lane offered, so no unreserved candidate is excluded at all, and no case stands up an oversize node whose unreserved lane is excluded on a different reason (`lane-gate: paused`, `availability: refused`, `budget-ceiling: …`) and requires codex to stay withheld, so a build that waives whenever every unreserved candidate is excluded — dropping the "only on context-fit" qualifier — passes all four cases and the negative control

findings.reason: a builder checking the premise by searching `_pick` finds nothing and must re-derive where `reasons` is consumed before it can confirm the note field is the right design; naming `pick()` at that line costs one edit and removes the search.
findings.text: §55 justifies the separate note field with "a candidate carrying any reason is excluded by `_pick`'s split", but no `_pick` exists anywhere under `reckon/crew/`; the split it names is `offered = [candidate for candidate in options if not candidate.reasons]` at `reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:404` inside `pick()`; the mechanism the sentence supports is correct, only the symbol is wrong

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §55 attributes the candidate split to `_pick`, a function that does not exist in `reckon/crew/picker/`; the split it describes is in `pick()` at `reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:404`. Every other anchor in both units resolves: `_reserved_lane_exclusion` (`reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:1186`), `candidates()` (`:1316`), `Candidate` (`reckon/crew/picker/types.py:26`), `_reserved_lane_exclusion`'s caller at `:1620`, `_record_pick_timings` (`reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:98`), the pick-timings log (`~/.config/reckon/crew/pick-timings.jsonl`, 16,992 rows), and both named test files (`tests/test_pick_records_its_stage_times.py`, `tests/test_hold_records_its_state.py`); §56's reason codes `context-fit`, `reserved-lane`, `budget-ceiling` (`snapshot.py:1173`, `:1223`, `:1234`, `:1239`), `availability` (`:1681`), `review-excluded-backend` and `in-harness-backend` (`:1523`, `:1530`, both colonless) are all real.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §55's four cases measure the "no unreserved candidate left" clause but none of them measures the "excluded only on `context-fit`" clause, so a waiver applied to any all-excluded candidate set passes every named case.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — neither section names a log path, but both name base and head arms run and compared, and the run-manifest contract every dispatched worker carries (`test_logs`, `baseline_suite`, a log whose last line is a bare `EXIT=<code>`) puts both logs under the run directory; §56 adds no scratch-tree measurement at all. Recorded as a note rather than a finding because the omission is silence, not a claim.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test filenames (`tests/test_an_oversize_node_reaches_a_reserved_lane.py`, `tests/test_a_refused_pick_records_its_exclusions.py`) and the waiver note text (`offered because no open lane fits the node's context`) all name the mechanism; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, a filename or a comment, and neither section carries changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §55's stated mechanism re-judges only the reserved-lane policy on the waiver path, but the candidate's own context fit it relies on is never computed for exactly the candidate being re-judged, because `_fit` is guarded by `if not reasons:` (`reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:1630-1636`) and a reserved candidate reaches that point with its tier reason already appended (`:1627-1629`). The two other checks hold: the root cause matches the cited evidence (the stated 58 refusals with `no-eligible-candidates; default-backend-ineligible` corroborated by 59 `refuse` rows carrying that exact reason in the same window of `~/.config/reckon/crew/pick-timings.jsonl`, reproduced against the local lane's own `usable_input_window: 230144`, `~/.config/reckon/flight.yaml:419-421`, and the codex floor `reasoning: [deep]` at `:72-75` which cannot express "too large for local", exactly as §55 says), and the mechanism's entry point, `candidates()` in `snapshot.py`, is the real caller that holds the whole candidate set. §56's mechanism runs on the real path: `excluded` is already built at `picker/__init__.py:405` before `_record_pick_timings` is called at `:508`, the resolved `estimate_out["tokens"]` is in the same scope, and `Selection.excluded` already returns the data the log lacks — so the section's premise ("records a refusal's outcome and a one-line reason, but not which lanes were excluded") reproduces.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §55 carries one deliverable (waive the reserved-lane tier and attempts terms for an oversize node) and §56 one (record the exclusions on a refused or fallen-back timing row).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §55 and §56 each declare no `plan-section-depends-on` entry and need none: §55 writes `snapshot.py` and `types.py`, §56 writes `picker/__init__.py`, the two share no write path, and §55's prerequisite (the host flight reserving codex with a `reasoning: [deep]` floor, `~/.config/reckon/flight.yaml:69-80`) is already declared on the host layer, whose own comment says "lane-and-model-routing carries that change". The one shared-write-path hazard, §53 and §55 both writing `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py`, was raised as wiring-1 and declined; §53's content and status are unchanged since, so it is not re-raised.
